summary: Adds asymmetric tenant placement assertions and workload-only, idempotent tenant lifecycle APIs while retaining placement v1 compatibility.
userImpact: Existing single-tenant and pooled installations continue to use their current routes and placement v1 configuration.
Cloud control planes can provision and operate tenants without acquiring an interactive user session.

instructions: No action is required for existing placement v1 installations.
Cloud pooled deployments configure the placement v2 JWKS, issuer, audience, shard identity, and workload receipt signing key before enabling the cloud-required profile.

configuration: Adds cloud-neutral placement v2 JWKS, issuer, audience, shard identity, and workload receipt signing settings.
Retains EG_TENANT_PLACEMENT_KEY and EG_TENANT_PLACEMENT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS for placement v1 during its compatibility window.

changes: Adds the placement-assertion/v2 header contract with ES256 key rotation and routing-bound claims.
Adds workload-only tenant create, suspend, resume, routing-alias reconciliation, and shard-readiness endpoints with idempotent signed receipts.

migrations: Migration 1700000000127-add-tenant-workload-lifecycle adds durable tenant lifecycle operation receipts and cloud-managed tenant routing aliases.
notes: The migration is additive and existing tenant, domain, session, and placement records are unchanged.

security: Placement v2 verifies ES256 assertions by public JWKS material and binds issuer, audience, tenant, shard, epoch, host, path, correlation, and validity window.
Tenant lifecycle endpoints accept only service-account credentials carrying the tenant lifecycle scope and never create browser sessions.
Lifecycle retries are request-hash bound and return signed, secret-free receipts.
Suspend and resume atomically advance the placement epoch so assertions minted before a lifecycle transition cannot be reused after reactivation.
documentation: Documents placement v2 configuration, workload lifecycle APIs, compatibility, rotation, and rollback.
knownLimitations: Placement v2 currently supports ES256; placement v1 HMAC remains available for compatibility.
rollback: Disable placement v2 and continue presenting placement v1 assertions while the compatibility window remains supported.
Roll back the application before removing the additive lifecycle-operation and routing-alias tables.
validation: Unit tests cover KMS-compatible ES256 fixtures, key rotation, claim and route mismatches, v1 compatibility, workload-only authentication, idempotency conflicts, signed receipts, and alias isolation.
Existing single-mode and pooled tenancy suites remain required.
